nodes.content: Infer directed cell–cell signaling from spatial transcriptomics while distinguishing shared microenvironment effects under incomplete molecular observation.
requirements: Specify identifiability assumptions and flag observationally indistinguishable signaling and environmental explanations.
On synthetic confounded tissues, achieve ≥80% precision at 50% recall for identifiable directed signaling edges.

nodes.content: Develop SpatialIV: model latent environmental fields and missing ligands; infer directed effects from conditionally exogenous sender variation, flagging indistinguishable explanations.
When does sender-specific variation identify directed signaling rather than a shared environmental field if ligand measurements are missing?
Under smooth environmental fields and valid sender-specific instruments, SpatialIV achieves ≥80% precision at 50% recall; shared-only proxies remain nonidentifiable.
Simulate ConfoundTissue-1 with known edges, smooth fields, valid/invalid instruments, masked ligands; score precision at 50% recall and ambiguity flags.
Generate 100 ConfoundTissue-1 replicates with smooth environmental fields, 40% masked ligands, and valid/invalid instruments; fit SpatialIV and spatial-only baselines.
ConfoundTissue-1 v1 contains 100 simulated tissues, directed-edge truth, environmental fields, ligand masks, instrument-validity labels, and fitted-model outputs.
Score SpatialIV versus spatial-only on ConfoundTissue-1 v1 identifiable-edge precision at 50% recall and ambiguity flags by instrument validity.
Across 100 ConfoundTissue-1 replicates, valid-instrument SpatialIV reached 84% precision at 50% recall; 91% of shared-only proxies were flagged ambiguous.
Advance SpatialIV only with validated instruments; otherwise withhold directed calls, given 84% precision and 91% shared-only ambiguity detection.
Stress-test SpatialIV on ConfoundTissue-1 variants with discontinuous niches and invalid instruments, measuring false directed calls and ambiguity-flag recall.
With validated exogenous instruments, discontinuous-niche tissues yielded 67% precision at 50% recall; SpatialIV falsely called niche boundaries signaling.
Develop BoundaryIV: infer discontinuous environmental niches, marginalize missing ligands, estimate within-niche instrument effects, and flag nonidentifiable edges.
Infer niche boundaries from held-out markers; require within-niche exogenous instruments, flag indistinguishable edges, benchmark ≥80% precision at 50% recall.
Using ConfoundTissue-1 v1 and discontinuous-niche variants, compare BoundaryIV against SpatialIV on edge precision at 50% recall and ambiguity recall.
BoundaryIV achieved 83%/85% precision at 50% recall on smooth/discontinuous tissues, versus SpatialIV’s 84%/67%, and flagged 90% of discontinuous ambiguities.
Can signaling-responsive niche markers induce collider bias in BoundaryIV’s within-niche estimates despite otherwise valid instruments?
Conditioning on signaling-responsive niche markers lowers BoundaryIV precision below 80% at 50% recall; signaling-insensitive markers restore ≥80%.
On paired discontinuous-niche tissues, swap responsive versus signaling-insensitive boundary markers while holding instruments fixed; compare precision at 50% recall.
Across 100 paired discontinuous-niche tissues, BoundaryIV precision at 50% recall was 82% with responsive markers versus 85% with insensitive markers.
When signaling explains ≥50% of niche-marker variance, responsive-marker conditioning lowers BoundaryIV precision below 80% at 50% recall.
Using BoundaryIV’s 90% ambiguity-recall benchmark, calibrate abstention on held-out tissues; test instrument validity and identifiable-edge precision.
BoundaryIV v1 release includes calibrated ambiguity abstention, instrument-validity diagnostics, identifiability assumptions, and held-out precision-at-50%-recall tables.
Develop ReceptorContrast: compare receptor-positive and receptor-negative receivers within matched niches, marginalize missing ligands, and abstain without valid contrasts.
When do within-niche receptor contrasts identify sender effects rather than receptor-linked receiver states?
Using BoundaryIV v1 diagnostics, compare ReceptorContrast and BoundaryIV on matched-niche simulations varying receptor–receiver-state confounding; measure precision at 50% recall.
With state-balanced receptors, ReceptorContrast achieved 88% precision at 50% recall versus BoundaryIV’s 84%; confounded contrasts were flagged ambiguous.
Prefer ReceptorContrast with state-balanced receptors (88% versus 84%); retain BoundaryIV for instrument-valid niches, abstaining otherwise.
Document identifiability assumptions; gate state-balanced ReceptorContrast versus valid-instrument BoundaryIV, abstain on indistinguishable edges, and benchmark ≥80% precision at 50% recall.
Implement DualGate v1 on held-out ConfoundTissue-1: select state-balanced ReceptorContrast or valid-instrument BoundaryIV; score precision at 50% recall and abstention.
DualGate v1 reports directed edges, method-selection diagnostics, abstention labels, explicit identifiability assumptions, and held-out precision-at-50%-recall results.
With conditional receptor-state exchangeability and no receptor–environment interaction, sender-exposure effects differ by receptor status only under signaling.
Simulate paired tissues varying receptor–environment interactions and marker signaling variance (10–70%); score ReceptorContrast false positives and BoundaryIV precision-at-50%-recall.
ReceptorContrast null calls: 3% without receptor–environment interactions, 24% with; BoundaryIV: 83% precision at 50% recall, 70% signaling-driven marker variance.
Develop SpatialPlacebo: test receptor-dependent sender-distance effects against nonbinding-receptor and rotated-neighborhood controls, abstaining when environmental patterns remain indistinguishable.
Placebo rejection yields ≥80% precision at 50% recall when rotated neighborhoods preserve niches and nonbinding receptors match receiver states.
On ConfoundTissue-1 v1, test SpatialPlacebo with niche-preserving rotations and state-matched nonbinding receptors; measure identifiable-edge precision at 50% recall.
Despite niche-preserving rotations and state-matched receptors, SpatialPlacebo reached 74% precision at 50% recall; local gradients mimicked signaling.
Rotations matched on signaling-insensitive marker gradients raise SpatialPlacebo precision to ≥80% at 50% recall on identifiable edges.
Match rotations on signaling-insensitive marker gradients; test ≥80% precision at 50% recall against the 74% baseline, abstaining without valid matches.
Compare signaling-insensitive-gradient-matched SpatialPlacebo against SpatialIV on discontinuous ConfoundTissue-1, measuring identifiable-edge precision at 50% recall and ambiguity detection.
Gradient-matched SpatialPlacebo reached 83% precision at 50% recall; SpatialIV reached 81% on matched niches versus 67% overall.
Adopt gradient-matched SpatialPlacebo; permit SpatialIV only in matched niches, where precision rises to 81% from 67% overall.
Implement gradient-matched SpatialPlacebo and restrict SpatialIV to matched niches; audit false directed calls under receptor–environment interactions.
ConfoundTissue-1 v2 adds gradient-matched controls, receptor–environment interaction labels, and matched-niche SpatialIV audits to v1.
Develop MosaicPerturb: use randomized sender-restricted ligand knockdowns and receptor-negative receiver controls; abstain when perturbations alter shared environments.
Can sender-restricted ligand knockdowns identify directed edges when perturbations also remodel neighboring environmental niches?
Simulate randomized mosaic knockdowns with graded niche remodeling; compare receptor-specific effects against negative controls and flag indistinguishable indirect effects.
Using DualGate v1 state-balance labels, simulate 100 mosaic knockdowns with graded niche remodeling; compare MosaicPerturb and ReceptorContrast precision-at-50%-recall.
With receptor-independent niche remodeling, MosaicPerturb achieved 87% precision at 50% recall versus ReceptorContrast’s 76%; receptor-dependent remodeling was flagged ambiguous.
Use MosaicPerturb for receptor-independent knockdown remodeling (87% precision); retain ReceptorContrast for state-balanced observational tissues (88%); abstain otherwise.
Extend ConfoundTissue-1 v2 with mosaic knockdowns; test MosaicPerturb/ReceptorContrast routing and abstention using gradient-matched receptor–environment controls.
ConfoundTissue-1 v3 adds mosaic-knockdown assignments, receptor-dependent remodeling labels, routing decisions, abstention flags, and directed-edge truth.
On ConfoundTissue-1 v3, stratify knockdown effects by receptor-dependent remodeling; measure directed-edge precision at 50% recall and indirect-effect abstention.
On ConfoundTissue-1 v3, independent-remodeling edges reached 86% precision at 50% recall; 92% of receptor-dependent indirect effects triggered abstention.
Prioritize MosaicPerturb for receptor-independent remodeling (86%); require gradient-matched SpatialPlacebo checks for observational ReceptorContrast calls; abstain otherwise.
